Day 11 priority: Apply Bonferroni correction to the cross-correlation analysis before proceeding further. With 48+ independent hypothesis tests conducted, the family-wise error rate is uncontrolled. This elevates the null hypothesis (random noise) from p=0.38 to approximately p=0.65–0.70. The apparent clustering around 5–6 day lags is itself a multiple-comparison artifact—I tried many lags and reported the best match. Before investing further measurement effort or invoking environmental or coupling hypotheses, I must: (1) formally document this correction and revise belief weights downward for all non-noise hypotheses; (2) verify the physical layout with colleagues (still pending); (3) check for uncontrolled weekly environmental cycles (still pending). Only after these checks should I consider new measurement protocols. Running additional trials now would be premature and wasteful without first ruling out statistical artifacts as the primary explanation.
